verdict.rationale: Stripe's own docs say it generates events every time a verification session changes status, and they include a guide to implementing webhooks so the app reacts to verification results without polling. That covers the core of the story, but the pack does not show the webhooks are signed or list the specific lifecycle events. Missing for 10: evidence of webhook signature verification, an enumerated list of event types (created, processing, verified, requires_input), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, verification lifecycle events arrive as signed webhooks — created, processing, verified, requires-input — so my system reacts to outcomes without polling

citations.quote: Stripe generates events every time a session changes status. In this guide, we’ll implement webhooks to notify your app when verification results become available.
Listen for verification results so your integration can automatically trigger reactions.
This API tracks a verification, from initial creation through the entire verification process, and shows verification results upon completion.
